title: Financial Goals
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 7 Pre-Technical Studies; not yet checked by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher; safety lines marked SAFETY in the library to confirm first; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Use shillings and amounts a Grade 7 learner might really save (pocket money, a chama, a school club). Never ask about a family's own income.

skills.key_step: The learner explains why financial goals matter (direction, discipline, saving, avoiding debt, meeting needs) and the factors when setting them: income, needs before wants, time available, cost of the item, savings already made, and changes in prices.
steps: Tell a goal from a wish.
contexts: a class saving for a ball
a chama saving for a water tank

board.say: What must be added to make this a goal?

board.do: Wait for the learner to say an amount, a plan and a date.

misconceptions.repair: Set a class goal: save 300 shillings for a football in 6 weeks; anyone with money can set goals.

misconceptions.ask: What makes a goal different from a wish?
misconceptions.repair: Turn a wish ("I want a bicycle") into a goal (amount, plan, date).

misconceptions.ask: A learner has little money. What comes first?
misconceptions.repair: Sort ten items into needs and wants; plan needs first.

misconceptions.ask: Which factor says how soon a goal can be reached?
misconceptions.repair: Compare saving 1,200 in 6 weeks and in 12 weeks with 100 a week; time changes what is possible.

checks.question: How is a goal different from a wish?
checks.answer: A goal has a plan and a date

checks.question: Name one factor in setting a financial goal.

skills.key_step: The learner tells a SMART financial goal (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic, Time-bound) from a weak one, and formulates one for themselves, such as "save 1,200 shillings in 12 weeks by saving 100 shillings a week for a school bag".

floor.prerequisite: Knows what a financial goal is.
floor.question: Is "save money" a goal or a wish?
floor.answer: A wish (it has no plan or date)

representations: SMART letters down the side of the board
contexts: a club saving for a trip
a youth saving for a sewing machine

board.do: Write the goal: "I will save more money."

board.say: Which SMART letters does it fail?

board.do: Wait for the learner to name specific, measurable and time-bound.
Rewrite it as a SMART goal.

misconceptions.ask: What does the A in SMART stand for?
misconceptions.repair: Write SMART down the side: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic, Time-bound; give an example for each.
Test "save more money" against each SMART letter; it fails four of them.

misconceptions.ask: A learner with 100 shillings a week aims to save 1 million shillings in a month. Is it SMART?
misconceptions.repair: Check a goal of 1 million in a month against income: not achievable or realistic.

misconceptions.ask: "I will save 500 shillings for a calculator." What is missing for it to be SMART?
misconceptions.repair: Tick each SMART letter for the goal; T has no tick. Add "within 10 weeks by saving 50 shillings a week".

checks.question: What does the T in SMART stand for?
Is "save more money" a SMART goal?
checks.answer: No, it is not specific, measurable or time-bound

skills.key_step: The learner works out simple money for a goal: weeks to reach a saving target (target ÷ weekly saving), profit on one item (selling price - buying price), total profit (profit per item × number sold).

floor.prerequisite: Can find profit on one sale.
floor.question: Buy for 40, sell for 55. Profit?

representations: a savings chart week by week

board.say: Which operation finds the number of weeks?

board.do: Wait for the learner to say divide.

misconceptions.ask: A trader buys a bag for 400 shillings and sells it for 500. What is the profit?
misconceptions.repair: Write profit = selling price - buying price; work three examples with real items.

misconceptions.ask: To save 1,200 shillings at 100 shillings a week, how many weeks are needed?
misconceptions.repair: Ask "how many 100s make 1,200?" with counters; that is division.

misconceptions.ask: A trader earns 10 shillings profit on each of 20 loaves. What is the total profit?
misconceptions.repair: Draw 20 loaves, each with 10 shillings profit; add them up, then multiply.
Always start from the money that came in (selling price), then take away the cost.

checks.question: Buy at 400, sell at 500. What is the profit?
Save 1,200 at 100 a week. How many weeks?
